_README: Hand-labelled verdicts for the ranking regression (#31), judged against
profile.example.yaml: Winter 2027 co-op, Toronto/Mississauga/Guelph,
hybrid or onsite, intern or junior, SQL/Python/Excel.
Every verdict below was decided by reading the posting against that profile,
NOT by running the scorer and writing down what it said. A label derived from
the thing under test measures nothing. Where the scorer disagrees with a
'pursue' or a 'skip', the label is the judgement and the scorer is wrong.
pursue     — I would spend an evening on this application.
skip       — I would not open it. Wrong country, wrong rung, or wrong job.
borderline — genuinely arguable. No ordering is asserted for these; they
are here so that a change which moves one is visible rather
than silent.
The test asserts only what the labels actually justify: no 'pursue' may be
cut by a hard filter, and no 'skip' may outrank a 'pursue'. It deliberately
does not assert exact scores -- pinning 0.62 would fail on every weight
change, including the improvements.
INCOMPLETE in the same way the extraction labels are: 12 postings, which is
enough to catch a rule that inverts the ranking and not enough to calibrate
one. Real calibration is outcome data (#4), which does not exist until
applications are out.
